Uptime Kuma 2.x → Unagikuma
===========================

                 1 maintenance window, 1 status page, 1 account
  Needs a look:  11 items (imported; see below)
  Not imported:  12 items (see below for what to do)

Needs a look (imported)
-----------------------
1. DNS default resolver (DNS) → dns-default-resolver
   Uptime Kuma asked the system's resolver; this check asks 1.1.1.1.
   To do: Change the target to your own DNS server if that is what you meant to
          watch.
2. gRPC users (gRPC) → grpc-users
   It uses the standard gRPC health check instead of a keyword match.
3. Mail server SMTP (TCP port) → mail-server-smtp
   Imported as a check that the mail port answers; the SMTP conversation is not
   checked.
4. Old site (paused) (HTTP) → old-site-paused
   It was paused in Uptime Kuma, so it is imported paused.
   To do: Resume it when you want it checked.
5. Switch uptime SNMP (SNMP) → switch-uptime-snmp
   It checks that the device answers SNMP; the OID value comparison is not
   carried over.
6. Tailscale node (Ping) → tailscale-node
   It is pinged directly, not through Tailscale.
   To do: Run Unagikuma (or a probe node) on a machine in your tailnet if the
          name only resolves there.
7. Channel "Team Slack" → team-slack
   Messages go to the webhook's own channel; the channel override (#alerts) is
   not used.
8. Channel "Generic webhook" → generic-webhook
   The message body differs from Uptime Kuma's.
   To do: Check that the receiving side understands it (Alerting › Channels ›
          Test).
9. Channel "Webhook custom body" → webhook-custom-body
   The message body differs from Uptime Kuma's. Its custom body template was not
   carried over (the template language differs).
   To do: Check that the receiving side understands it (Alerting › Channels ›
          Test). Write the body again under Alerting › Channels (body=).
10. Channel "Ops email" → ops-email
    Copy (CC/BCC) addresses are sent to as normal recipients.
11. Status page "Public status" → public
    Its monitors are shown in one list; the sections of the Uptime Kuma page are
    not kept.

Not imported
------------
1. Minecraft server (Game server)
   Why: Unagikuma has no game-server query.
   To do: Check the server's port with a TCP or UDP monitor.
2. Mongo (MongoDB)
   Why: Unagikuma has no MongoDB check.
   To do: Check port 27017 with a TCP monitor, or run a script check (EXEC).
3. MQTT sensors (MQTT)
   Why: Unagikuma has no MQTT check.
   To do: Check the broker port with a TCP monitor, or have the device call a
          push URL (a Push monitor).
4. MSSQL (SQL Server)
   Why: Unagikuma has no SQL Server check.
   To do: Check port 1433 with a TCP monitor, or run a script check (EXEC).
5. Old host must be down (HTTP)
   Why: It is in upside-down mode (it is up when the service is down). Unagikuma
        has no such mode, so it would report the opposite.
   To do: If you still need it, add it by hand as a normal check and decide what
          “up” should mean.
6. RabbitMQ (RabbitMQ)
   Why: Unagikuma has no RabbitMQ check.
   To do: Check the management API with an HTTP monitor, or port 5672 with a TCP
          monitor.
7. RADIUS (RADIUS)
   Why: Unagikuma cannot log in to RADIUS.
   To do: Check that the server answers with a UDP monitor on port radius
          (1812).
8. Steam game server (Steam game server)
   Why: Unagikuma has no Steam server query.
   To do: Check the server's port with a TCP or UDP monitor.
9. Websocket (WebSocket)
   Why: Unagikuma has no WebSocket check.
   To do: Check the server with an HTTP or TCP monitor.
10. Group "Empty group"
    Why: The group has no monitors that were imported.
    To do: Nothing to do: groups appear here as soon as a monitor uses them
           (group=).
11. Channels: Pushover (Pushover), Teams (Microsoft Teams), Gotify (Gotify),
    PagerDuty (PagerDuty), Unused Matrix (Matrix)
    Why: No imported monitor uses them.
    To do: Add them under Alerting › Channels if you still need them.
12. Maintenance "Manual maintenance"
    Why: It is switched on and off by hand, which has no schedule to copy. It
         was on when exported.
    To do: Silence the monitors (Problems › Silence) or announce the work under
           Notices & status › Changes.

Good to know
------------
- Past checks, uptime history and incidents stay in Uptime Kuma: history starts
  fresh here.
- Credentials (tokens, passwords, webhook addresses) are stored as encrypted
  secrets, not in the configuration file.
